status.main_product: Industrial AI and asset inspection software (DetectOS and T-Pulse)
status.scope_reason: The company delivers aerial drone inspections, asset management, and vegetation-clearance analysis through its specialized utility asset inspection platform, DetectOS.
status.evidence: According to Ministry of Corporate Affairs records updated in September 2026, Detect Technologies Private Limited is active and headquartered in Chennai, India, while its official website details its core execution of drone-powered powerline inspections and vegetation analytics via its DetectOS platform.

claims.claim: The company reports utilizing its autonomous industrial UAV, Noctua DAX, for asset inspections, and field data shows its operators deploy DJI M30T and M300 platforms for visual utility infrastructure data collection.
The company has deployed drone-based infrared thermal cameras for health condition assessments of 33 KV power cables in a project for IndianOil.

The company reports its T-Pulse flagship cloud-based SaaS platform utilizes automated machine vision models to achieve up to 98.4% detection accuracy for safety, operational, and asset inspection monitoring.
The company optimized its 3D modeling and photogrammetry workflows by integrating platform-ready meshes with software tools like Blender and Meshroom to minimize visual fidelity loss.
claims.note: minimizing visual fidelity loss via platform-ready meshes

claims.claim: The company reports that its DetectOS asset management platform processed 120,000 drone inspection images across 2,600 transmission towers within 25 days, enabling AI-powered defect detection in transmission hardware and real-time mapping.
The company reports that its DetectOS platform enabled a utility to capture and process 120,000 drone inspection images across 2,600 transmission towers within a 25-day period.

claims.parameter: Utility Digital Twin & Predictive Maintenance Platform
claims.claim: The company reports that its T-Pulse platform has been used to inspect over 9,000 components per 100 kilometers on transmission lines and extra-high voltage (EHV) towers, utilizing AI algorithms to mine asset degradation information and deliver maintenance recommendations.
claims.note: 9,000 components per 100 kilometers on transmission lines

claims.parameter: Revenue & Growth in Indian Power Sector
claims.claim: Detect Technologies Pvt. Ltd. reported a total company operating revenue of ₹51.0 Cr for the financial year ending March 31, 2025 (FY25), representing an increase of 41.8% from ₹35.9 Cr in FY24.

claims.parameter: Revenue & Growth in Indian Power Sector
claims.claim: Elevation Capital reported that the company's drone product NOCTUA and SaaS platforms serve multiple process industries, including the power sector, but specific regional or sector breakdowns are not public.

Detect Technologies Pvt. Ltd. obtained initial type-level registration under previous frameworks for its "NOCTUA DS" drone model, recorded with a maximum take-off weight of 1.85 kg and an attainable height of 2,624 feet.

The company actively employs Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) certified pilots and operations staff to manage regulatory compliance and onsite flight logistics for industrial utility asset inspection workflows.

The company reports running the Detect Partner Network, a community of qualified third-party drone pilots and drone service providers who fly the utility inspection workloads won by Detect, which is managed via their data quality program and the DetectOS portal.

Ltd., Chennai, India, though they originate from shared roots or closely related naming, the utility grid inspection platform DetectOS is operated by the US entity Detect Technologies LLC/Inc.

claims.claim: Detect Technologies Pvt. Ltd. signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Engineers India Limited (EIL) on April 12, 2024, to collaborate on offering real-time artificial intelligence-based safety and progress monitoring solutions utilizing cameras and drones at construction sites for various domestic and international projects.

The company reports a technology partnership with Zeus Solutions Inc. announced in mid-2026 to integrate AI-powered industrial intelligence and real-time operational insights for workplace safety and enterprise-scale inspections.
